messages.subject: scoring with insufficient response categories in the response data
parts: I am trying to use mirt to do scoring (only estimate the ability parameters and fix the item parameters). In my data, I have two dichotomous items with only one response category in the response data. What shall I do in this case to include the two items for scoring?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: scoring with insufficient response categories in the response data
parts:
The data used to define your mirt model isn't really relevant if the IRT parameters are fixed and known. See this post: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/34119/estimating-ability-using-irt-when-the-model-parameters-are-known/48105#48105

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: scoring with insufficient response categories in the response data
parts:
You feed the response data to the fscores() function via the input response.pattern. Give the CV post a good look over, and track what's happening to the object names. 

#########
sv <- mirt(Science, 1, pars = 'values')
# edit some data
## 
##
sv$est <- FALSE

mod <- mirt(Science, 1, pars=sv)
fscores(mod, response.pattern = rbind(c(1,2,3,4), 
  c(4,3,2,1)))
##

Phil

It requires some math translations to take the classical form and put it into the slope-intercept. You can save yourself a bit of time by using the internal (and therefore, undocumented) traditional2mirt() function.

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/mirt-package/gpcmIRT$20itemtype$20for$20the$20generate_mirt_object$20method%7Csort:date/mirt-package/HaECnkrvV-E/qrR0dyy3BAAJ
